```md docs/project-manager-summary.md
We defined the codx-junior **@project_manager**: an agile (Kanban-first) profile that keeps tasks updated, organized and delivered, tackling the task-volume challenge of hybrid AI + human teams.
It is the first **background profile**, running on a user-configured cron schedule via a new `project_manager` module, and operating exclusively through an auditable set of task management tools.
Data model extensions were proposed: `last_check`, `pm_state`, `priority`, `due_date`, `assignees`, `origin` on tasks, plus new `PMFollowUp`, `PMRunReport` and `ProfileBackground` models.
Team interactions are handled via tracked follow-ups (request → remind → escalate/auto-resolve) with notification rate limits; v1 reacts only to cron runs and mentions, deferring chat-event reactions to v2.
A 5-phase implementation roadmap was created (foundations, PM module & tools, follow-ups, agility metrics, event-driven v2), documented in `docs/project-manager.md`.
```

# codx-junior Project Manager (PM)

Based on my investigation of the codebase, here's how tasks and chats are managed today, followed by the full definition of the PM role.

## Investigation Summary: How Tasks & Chats Work in codx-junior

**Key findings:**

| Concept | Implementation |
|---------|----------------|
| **Task = Chat** | Tasks are `Chat` objects (`codx/junior/db.py`) stored as JSON files under `.codx/tasks/{board}/{column}/{name}.{id}.json` |
| **Organization** | Kanban-style: `board` + `column` fields (defaults: board=`kanban`, column=`tasks`). `Board`/`Column` models in `model/model.py` |
| **Hierarchy** | `parent_id` links sub-tasks to parent chats; `generate_tasks()` (`chat_engine_actions.py`) splits a chat into AI-generated sub-tasks |
| **Status & tracking** | `Chat.status`, `updated_at`, `users`, `profiles`, `check_lists`, `chat_index`; `TaskGenerationStatus` tracks generation progress |
| **Profiles** | `Profile` model (`model/model.py`) with `name`, `content` (instructions), `category`, `llm_model`, `tools`; managed by `ProfileManager`; invoked via `@mentions` |
| **Background activity** | `background.py` runs daemon loops (`check_projects`, `check_projects_wiki`) with quarantine/retry logic, thread pools, and configurable intervals |
| **Agents** | `AgentBase` (`agents/base_agent.py`) wraps a `CODXJuniorSession`; e.g. `GitIssuesAgent`, `DevOpsAgent` |
| **Events** | `EventManager` + `SessionChannel` (Socket.IO) broadcast `chat_event` / `message_event` for real-time updates |

With this, here is the PM definition document:

```md docs/project-manager.md
# codx-junior Project Manager (PM)

The **Project Manager (PM)** is a codx-junior profile with background activity,
responsible for keeping the project's task boards healthy: tasks updated,
organized, unblocked and delivered on time.

---

## 1. Overview

In codx-junior, **tasks are chats**. Every task lives as a `Chat` stored under
`.codx/tasks/{board}/{column}/`, organized in Kanban boards and columns.
The PM operates on top of this system:

- As a **profile** (`@pm`), it can be mentioned in any chat to get project
  management assistance (planning, prioritization, status reports).
- As a **background activity**, it periodically reviews all boards, detects
  stale or blocked tasks, and involves team members to protect deadlines.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PM[PM Profile + Background Activity]
    PM --> Review[Review task boards]
    PM --> Organize[Organize & prioritize]
    PM --> Follow[Follow up stale tasks]
    PM --> Involve[Involve team members]
    PM --> Report[Status reports]
    Review --> ChatManager[ChatManager: list_chats]
    Involve --> Events[EventManager: notifications]
    Report --> Boards[Kanban boards & columns]
```

---

## 2. Role Definition

> The PM is the guardian of the project's delivery flow. It never writes code;
> it makes sure the right tasks are visible, well-defined, assigned, and moving.

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Profile name | `pm` |
| Category | `project` |
| Invocation | `@pm` mention in any chat |
| Background | Yes — periodic board review loop |
| Scope | All boards and columns of the project |

---

## 3. Responsibilities

### 3.1 Task hygiene
- Ensure every task (chat) has a clear `name`, `description` and column.
- Detect tasks with missing or vague descriptions and refine them
  (same mechanism used by `generate_tasks` sub-task refinement).
- Keep `check_lists` updated as acceptance criteria.

### 3.2 Board organization
- Keep tasks in the correct `board`/`column` reflecting their real state
  (e.g. `tasks` → `in-progress` → `review` → `done`).
- Detect duplicated or overlapping tasks and propose merges (via `parent_id`
  or `linked_chat_ids`).
- Split oversized tasks into sub-tasks using the task generation flow.

### 3.3 Status review & follow-up
- Review `updated_at` on all tasks: flag tasks with no activity beyond a
  configurable threshold (default: 48h) as **stale**.
- Track tasks by `status` and column to build the project's delivery picture.
- Detect blocked tasks (error messages, unanswered questions, unfinished
  agent runs via `lifecycle_events`).

### 3.4 Team involvement
- Identify the `users` involved in each task and notify them when:
  - a task assigned to them is stale,
  - a task is waiting for their answer (last message not from them),
  - a deadline is at risk.
- Notifications are sent through `EventManager.send_notification` and
  chat messages mentioning the user.

### 3.5 Reporting
- Produce a periodic **Project Status Report** as a pinned chat in a
  dedicated `pm` board, including:
  - tasks per column (backlog / in progress / done),
  - stale & blocked tasks,
  - recently completed work,
  - risks and suggested next actions.

---

## 4. Way of Working

### 4.1 Interactive mode (profile mention)

Any user can mention `@pm` in a chat. Examples:

```text
@pm what's the current status of the kanban board?
@pm this task is too big, split it and assign the pieces
@pm generate the weekly status report
```

When mentioned, the PM receives its profile `content` as instructions
(standard profile mechanism in `ChatEngine.get_query_mentions`), plus the
chat context, and answers with project-management focus.

### 4.2 Background mode

The PM background activity follows the same pattern as existing background
services (`codx/junior/background.py`):

1. **Loop** — runs for every project with `pm` profile enabled, on a
   configurable interval (suggested default: 30 minutes, similar to
   `WIKI_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS`).
2. **Scan** — uses `ChatManager.list_chats(from_date=...)` to load task
   metadata (cheap: `chat_only`, no messages).
3. **Analyze** — classifies tasks: `ok`, `stale`, `blocked`, `unassigned`,
   `misplaced` (wrong column vs. actual state).
4. **Act** —
   - posts follow-up messages on stale/blocked tasks mentioning involved users,
   - proposes column moves (or applies them if auto-mode is enabled),
   - updates the Project Status Report chat.
5. **Notify** — emits events through `EventManager` / `SessionChannel` so the
   UI reflects changes in real time.
6. **Quarantine-safe** — respects the existing quarantine/backoff mechanism
   to avoid hammering failing projects.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant BG as Background Loop
    participant CM as ChatManager
    participant AI as AI (pm profile)
    participant EM as EventManager

    BG->>CM: list_chats() (metadata only)
    BG->>BG: classify tasks (stale/blocked/ok)
    BG->>AI: analyze flagged tasks + build report
    AI-->>BG: actions & report content
    BG->>CM: save_chat (follow-ups, report)
    BG->>EM: chat_event / send_notification
```

### 4.3 Decision boundaries

| The PM does | The PM does NOT |
|-------------|-----------------|
| Update task metadata (column, description, checklists) | Write or modify project code |
| Post follow-up messages and reports | Delete tasks or chats |
| Notify and involve users | Impersonate users |
| Propose task splits/merges | Force-close tasks without confirmation |

---

## 5. PM Profile Definition

The PM is registered like any other profile (see `software_developer.profile`):

Your mission is to keep the task boards healthy and the team unblocked.\n\nResponsibilities:\n* Review all tasks (chats) and their status: name, description, column, users, last update.\n* Detect stale tasks (no updates for more than 48h) and blocked tasks (errors, unanswered questions).\n* Keep tasks in the correct board column reflecting their real state.\n* Ensure every task has a clear name, an actionable description and acceptance criteria (checklists).\n* Split oversized tasks into sub-tasks; link related tasks.\n* Involve team members: mention users when their input is needed or a deadline is at risk.\n* Produce concise status reports: tasks per column, stale/blocked items, completed work, risks and next actions.\n\nRules:\n* Never write or modify project code.\n* Never delete tasks; propose archiving instead.\n* Be concise, actionable and factual. Always reference task names and users.\n* When proposing changes (column moves, splits, merges), list them clearly so they can be confirmed or auto-applied."

```

---

## 6. Configuration (proposed)

Settings to control the PM background activity:

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `pm_enabled` | `false` | Enable PM background loop for the project |
| `pm_check_interval_seconds` | `1800` | Time between board reviews |
| `pm_stale_task_hours` | `48` | Hours without update before a task is stale |
| `pm_auto_apply` | `false` | Auto-apply column moves vs. propose only |
| `pm_report_board` | `pm` | Board where status reports are stored |

---

## 7. Integration Points

| Component | Usage by PM |
|-----------|-------------|
| `ChatManager` | List/load/save task chats; move between columns |
| `ProfileManager` | Load the `pm` profile instructions |
| `background.py` | Host the PM review loop (new `check_projects_pm` thread) |
| `EventManager` / `SessionChannel` | Real-time notifications and board updates |
| `generate_tasks` (`chat_engine_actions.py`) | Split large tasks into sub-tasks |
| `AgentBase` | Optional `PMAgent` implementation for the background logic |

Here's the complete revised document, incorporating all your notes: renamed to `@project_manager`, tools-based, agile-focused, background profile type with cron, data model analysis, team interactions, and chat events — all packaged as an implementation roadmap.

```md docs/project-manager.md
# codx-junior Project Manager (@project_manager)

The **Project Manager** is a codx-junior profile responsible for keeping the
project's tasks healthy: updated, organized, unblocked and delivered on time.

It is the first **background profile**: besides answering mentions like any
other profile, it runs autonomously on a schedule to review and organize the
project boards.

> **The challenge**: hybrid AI + human teams generate tasks at a rate no human
> PM can follow. Every conversation can spawn sub-tasks, every agent can open
> work items. The @project_manager's mission is to keep this ever-growing
> backlog organized, prioritized and moving — using well-known agile
> practices, not reinventing project management.

---

## 1. Role Definition

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Profile name | `project_manager` |
| Mention | `@project_manager` |
| Category | `project` |
| Type | Background profile (cron-scheduled) + interactive |
| Powers | Task management tools (read/update/organize tasks, notify users) |
| Boundaries | Never writes code, never deletes tasks, never impersonates users |

### Mission

> Guardian of the delivery flow. Makes sure the right tasks are visible,
> well-defined, assigned and moving — and that humans and AI agents always
> know what to do next.

---

## 2. Responsibilities

### 2.1 Keep tasks updated
- Ensure every task has a clear **title**, **description**, and **acceptance
  criteria** (checklists).
- Detect tasks that lack information and ask the creator to clarify.
- Update task status when reality diverges from the board (e.g. a task with
  recent activity still sitting in "backlog").
- Record its own review activity so every task carries a "last checked by PM"
  trail.

### 2.2 Organize the boards (the volume problem)
- **Triage**: new tasks are classified — is it actionable? duplicated? too big?
- **Deduplicate**: detect overlapping tasks, propose merges or linking.
- **Split**: break oversized tasks into sub-tasks with clear scope.
- **Tag**: apply consistent tags (area, priority, type) so tasks are findable.
- **Prioritize**: keep columns ordered by priority; keep WIP limits visible.
- **Archive proposals**: flag abandoned tasks for archiving (never deletes).

### 2.3 Follow up & unblock
- Detect **stale** tasks (no activity beyond a threshold).
- Detect **blocked** tasks (waiting for an answer, failed agent run, unresolved
  question).
- Follow up on the task itself and involve the right people.

### 2.4 Involve team members
- Notify users when their input is needed or a deadline is at risk.
- Track pending requests: who was asked what, when, and whether they answered.

### 2.5 Report
- Maintain a periodic **Status Report**: work in progress, completed, stale,
  blocked, risks and suggested next actions.

---

## 3. Agile Way of Working

The @project_manager applies classic agile practices, adapted to hybrid teams:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Inbox[Inbox / New tasks] -->|Triage| Backlog
    Backlog -->|Prioritize| Ready
    Ready -->|Assign| InProgress[In Progress]
    InProgress -->|Follow up| Review
    Review --> Done
    InProgress -.->|Stale / Blocked| FollowUp[PM Follow-up]
    FollowUp -.-> InProgress
```

### 3.1 Continuous triage (Kanban-first)
Because tasks arrive continuously (from humans and AI), the PM works
**Kanban-style** rather than sprint-batch:

1. **Inbox zero**: every new task gets triaged on the next PM run — classified,
   tagged, and placed in the right column, or sent back with questions.
2. **Definition of Ready**: a task only moves to "Ready" when it has title,
   description, acceptance criteria and priority.
3. **WIP awareness**: the PM reports when too many tasks are in progress per
   person/agent and suggests focusing.
4. **Definition of Done**: tasks are only "Done" when acceptance criteria
   (checklists) are complete; otherwise the PM asks.

### 3.2 Cadences (agile ceremonies, async)
Ceremonies become scheduled background runs:

| Ceremony | PM equivalent | Suggested cadence |
|----------|---------------|-------------------|
| Daily standup | Stale/blocked review + follow-ups | Daily (cron) |
| Backlog refinement | Triage, dedupe, split, tag | Every run |
| Sprint review | Status Report | Weekly (cron) |
| Retrospective | Flow metrics summary (cycle time, throughput, stale rate) | Weekly/monthly |

### 3.3 Handling the volume (AI + human hybrid teams)
Strategies specifically for the task-explosion problem:

- **Hierarchy first**: sub-tasks always linked to parents; the PM reports at
  parent level, details on demand.
- **Aggressive tagging**: consistent tags are the only way to slice hundreds
  of tasks; the PM owns the tag taxonomy.
- **Auto-expiry proposals**: tasks untouched for N days get a follow-up; still
  untouched after the grace period → proposed for archive.
- **AI-generated task quality gate**: tasks created by agents get extra triage
  scrutiny (dedupe check, scope check) before entering the backlog.
- **Summarize, don't enumerate**: reports show aggregates and top-N exceptions,
  never full task dumps.

---

## 4. Data Model Analysis

To support the PM strategy, the current task/chat model needs extensions.
Analysis of what's needed:

### 4.1 Task-level fields (extend `Chat`)

| Field | Type | Purpose | Status |
|-------|------|---------|--------|
| `status` | enum | Exists but needs a defined lifecycle: `new`, `ready`, `in-progress`, `blocked`, `review`, `done`, `archived` | **Extend/formalize** |
| `tags` | `list[str]` | Exists — PM owns taxonomy conventions (`prio:high`, `type:bug`, `area:api`, ...) | **Reuse** |
| `last_check` | datetime | When the PM last reviewed this task | **New** |
| `pm_state` | object | PM's assessment: `{ health: ok\|stale\|blocked\|needs-info, last_action, next_check }` | **New** |
| `priority` | enum/int | Explicit priority (`critical`/`high`/`normal`/`low`) instead of tag-only | **New** |
| `due_date` | datetime | Deadline tracking — core to "guarantee deadlines" | **New** |
| `assignees` | `list[str]` | Explicit ownership (users field exists but means "participants") | **New/clarify** |
| `origin` | enum | `human` \| `ai-agent` \| `pm` — needed for the AI quality gate | **New** |

### 4.2 Follow-up tracking (new model)

To "keep track of communications with team members" the PM needs a record of
pending requests:

```python
class PMFollowUp(BaseModel):
    id: str
    task_id: str
    requested_from: str          # user or agent
    request: str                 # what was asked
    requested_at: datetime
    remind_after_hours: int = 24
    reminders_sent: int = 0
    status: str = "pending"      # pending | answered | escalated | expired
    resolved_at: Optional[datetime]
```

### 4.3 Background profile configuration (extend `Profile`)

```python
class ProfileBackground(BaseModel):
    enabled: bool = False
    cron: str = "0 * * * *"      # standard cron expression
    last_run: Optional[datetime]
    last_run_status: str = ""    # ok | error
    max_run_seconds: int = 300   # safety timeout
```

`Profile` gains: `background: Optional[ProfileBackground]`. Any profile can
become a background profile; `project_manager` is the first one.

### 4.4 PM run log (new model)

Auditability — what the PM did on each run:

```python
class PMRunReport(BaseModel):
    run_at: datetime
    tasks_reviewed: int
    tasks_updated: int
    follow_ups_created: int
    notifications_sent: int
    actions: list[str]           # human-readable action log
    metrics: dict                # throughput, cycle time, stale count...
```

---

## 5. Task Management Tools

The PM operates exclusively through a **tool set** (no direct data access from
prompts). This makes actions auditable and reusable by other profiles later.

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `list_tasks(filters)` | Query tasks by board, column, status, tags, assignee, staleness |
| `get_task(task_id)` | Full task detail including checklists and activity |
| `update_task(task_id, fields)` | Update title, description, status, tags, priority, due_date, column |
| `create_task(...)` | Create a task (e.g. splitting a big one) |
| `link_tasks(parent_id, child_ids)` | Build/maintain task hierarchy |
| `add_checklist(task_id, items)` | Set acceptance criteria |
| `comment_task(task_id, message, mentions)` | Post a follow-up message, mentioning users |
| `create_follow_up(task_id, user, request)` | Register a tracked request to a team member |
| `resolve_follow_up(follow_up_id)` | Mark a request as answered |
| `notify_user(user, message, task_id)` | Direct notification |
| `get_board_metrics(board)` | Aggregates: counts per column, stale, cycle time |
| `publish_report(content)` | Create/update the Status Report |

---

## 6. Background Profiles & the project_manager Module

### 6.1 Background profiles (new concept)

A **background profile** is a profile that runs unattended on a schedule.

**Background rules (v1):**
1. Scheduling is a plain **cron expression** configured by the user on the
   profile (`background.cron`).
2. One run at a time per project (no overlapping runs).
3. Runs have a **timeout** (`max_run_seconds`) and are killed if exceeded.
4. Failed runs are logged and retried on next schedule (no immediate retry);
   repeated failures put the profile in quarantine with backoff.
5. Every run produces a **run report** visible to the user.
6. Background runs use only the profile's **tools** — no free-form side
   effects.
7. Users can trigger a manual run anytime ("Run now").

**Future modes** (out of scope for v1): event-driven runs, adaptive
scheduling based on activity volume.

### 6.2 The `project_manager` module

New module hosting the PM background logic:

```
codx/junior/project_manager/
├── __init__.py
├── pm_agent.py          # PM run orchestration: scan → analyze → act → report
├── tools.py             # Task management tool implementations
├── follow_ups.py        # Follow-up tracking (create, remind, escalate)
├── metrics.py           # Board/flow metrics computation
├── scheduler.py         # Cron evaluation & background run entry point
└── models.py            # PMFollowUp, PMRunReport, PM settings
```

**Run cycle:**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant SCHED as Scheduler (cron)
    participant PM as PM Agent
    participant TOOLS as PM Tools
    participant AI as LLM (project_manager profile)
    participant TEAM as Team members

    SCHED->>PM: trigger run
    PM->>TOOLS: list_tasks (changed since last_check)
    PM->>PM: classify (new / stale / blocked / ok / done-check)
    PM->>AI: analyze exceptions + propose actions
    AI-->>PM: actions (updates, splits, follow-ups, report)
    PM->>TOOLS: apply actions
    TOOLS->>TEAM: comments, mentions, notifications
    PM->>TOOLS: publish_report + run log
```

The scan is **incremental**: only tasks changed since `last_check` (plus tasks
whose `pm_state.next_check` is due) are analyzed — essential for large boards.

---

## 7. Interactions with Team Members

### 7.1 How @project_manager requests actions

When the PM needs something from a team member (human or agent):

1. **Comment on the task** mentioning the user with a **specific, answerable
   request**: *"@alice this task has no acceptance criteria — can you confirm
   the expected behavior for X?"*
2. **Register a follow-up** (`create_follow_up`) with a reminder deadline.
3. **Notify** the user through the app notification channel.

### 7.2 Tracking communications

Every request is a tracked `PMFollowUp`:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> pending: request created
    pending --> answered: user responds
    pending --> pending: reminder sent (after remind_after_hours)
    pending --> escalated: N reminders without answer
    escalated --> answered: user responds
    escalated --> expired: grace period ends
    answered --> [*]
    expired --> [*]: task flagged / archive proposed
```

- **Answered detection**: when the mentioned user posts on the task after the
  request, the follow-up is auto-resolved (PM verifies the answer addresses
  the request on next run).
- **Escalation**: after N unanswered reminders, the PM raises visibility —
  flags the task, includes it in the Status Report's risk section, and (if
  configured) notifies a project owner.
- **Respect limits**: max reminders per follow-up and per user per day, to
  avoid notification fatigue.

### 7.3 Requesting actions from AI agents

The PM treats AI profiles as team members: it can mention them
(`@software_developer please pick up this ready task`) — enabling PM-driven
work dispatch in the future.

---

## 8. Chat Events — Should the PM React?

Analysis of event-driven vs. scheduled behavior:

| Event | React immediately? | Rationale |
|-------|-------------------|-----------|
| **Mention** (`@project_manager`) | ✅ Yes (v1) | Standard profile behavior — user expects an answer |
| Task **created** | ❌ v1: next cron run / ✅ v2: lightweight triage | Immediate triage of every AI-generated task would be noisy and expensive; batching in cron runs handles volume better |
| Task **updated** | ❌ No | Would create feedback loops (PM updates trigger PM); the incremental scan covers it |
| **Message added** on task with pending follow-up | ✅ v2 | Cheap, valuable: auto-resolve follow-ups in near-real-time |
| Task moved to **done** | ❌ v1 / ✅ v2 | Done-criteria verification fits the cron run in v1 |

**Decision**: v1 is **cron-only + mentions**. Event reactions are v2, and only
for cheap, non-LLM operations (follow-up resolution) or explicitly configured
triggers. This keeps costs predictable and avoids event storms from
high-volume hybrid teams.

---

## 9. Profile Definition

It is the first **background profile**: besides answering mentions like any
other profile, it runs autonomously on a schedule to review and organize the
project boards.

> **The challenge**: hybrid AI + human teams generate tasks at a rate no human
> PM can follow. Every conversation can spawn sub-tasks, every agent can open
> work items. The @project_manager's mission is to keep this ever-growing
> backlog organized, prioritized and moving — using well-known agile
> practices, not reinventing project management.

## 1. Role Definition

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Profile name | `project_manager` |
| Mention | `@project_manager` |
| Category | `project` |
| Type | Background profile (cron-scheduled) + interactive |
| Powers | Task management tools (read/update/organize tasks, notify users) |
| Boundaries | Never writes code, never deletes tasks, never impersonates users |

### Mission

> Guardian of the delivery flow. Makes sure the right tasks are visible,
> well-defined, assigned and moving — and that humans and AI agents always
> know what to do next.

## 2. Responsibilities

### 2.1 Keep tasks updated
- Ensure every task has a clear **title**, **description**, and **acceptance
  criteria** (checklists).
- Detect tasks that lack information and ask the creator to clarify.
- Update task status when reality diverges from the board (e.g. a task with
  recent activity still sitting in "backlog").
- Record its own review activity so every task carries a "last checked by PM"
  trail.

### 2.2 Organize the boards (the volume problem)
- **Triage**: new tasks are classified — is it actionable? duplicated? too big?
- **Deduplicate**: detect overlapping tasks, propose merges or linking.
- **Split**: break oversized tasks into sub-tasks with clear scope.
- **Tag**: apply consistent tags (area, priority, type) so tasks are findable.
- **Prioritize**: keep columns ordered by priority; keep WIP limits visible.
- **Archive proposals**: flag abandoned tasks for archiving (never deletes).

### 2.3 Follow up & unblock
- Detect **stale** tasks (no activity beyond a threshold).
- Detect **blocked** tasks (waiting for an answer, failed agent run, unresolved
  question).
- Follow up on the task itself and involve the right people.

### 2.4 Involve team members
- Notify users when their input is needed or a deadline is at risk.
- Track pending requests: who was asked what, when, and whether they answered.

### 2.5 Report
- Maintain a periodic **Status Report**: work in progress, completed, stale,
  blocked, risks and suggested next actions.

## 3. Agile Way of Working

The @project_manager applies classic agile practices, adapted to hybrid teams:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Inbox[Inbox / New tasks] -->|Triage| Backlog
    Backlog -->|Prioritize| Ready
    Ready -->|Assign| InProgress[In Progress]
    InProgress -->|Follow up| Review
    Review --> Done
    InProgress -.->|Stale / Blocked| FollowUp[PM Follow-up]
    FollowUp -.-> InProgress
```

### 3.1 Continuous triage (Kanban-first)
Because tasks arrive continuously (from humans and AI), the PM works
**Kanban-style** rather than sprint-batch:

1. **Inbox zero**: every new task gets triaged on the next PM run — classified,
   tagged, and placed in the right column, or sent back with questions.
2. **Definition of Ready**: a task only moves to "Ready" when it has title,
   description, acceptance criteria and priority.
3. **WIP awareness**: the PM reports when too many tasks are in progress per
   person/agent and suggests focusing.
4. **Definition of Done**: tasks are only "Done" when acceptance criteria
   (checklists) are complete; otherwise the PM asks.

### 3.2 Cadences (agile ceremonies, async)
Ceremonies become scheduled background runs:

| Ceremony | PM equivalent | Suggested cadence |
|----------|---------------|-------------------|
| Daily standup | Stale/blocked review + follow-ups | Daily (cron) |
| Backlog refinement | Triage, dedupe, split, tag | Every run |
| Sprint review | Status Report | Weekly (cron) |
| Retrospective | Flow metrics summary (cycle time, throughput, stale rate) | Weekly/monthly |

### 3.3 Handling the volume (AI + human hybrid teams)
Strategies specifically for the task-explosion problem:

- **Hierarchy first**: sub-tasks always linked to parents; the PM reports at
  parent level, details on demand.
- **Aggressive tagging**: consistent tags are the only way to slice hundreds
  of tasks; the PM owns the tag taxonomy.
- **Auto-expiry proposals**: tasks untouched for N days get a follow-up; still
  untouched after the grace period → proposed for archive.
- **AI-generated task quality gate**: tasks created by agents get extra triage
  scrutiny (dedupe check, scope check) before entering the backlog.
- **Summarize, don't enumerate**: reports show aggregates and top-N exceptions,
  never full task dumps.

## 4. Data Model Analysis

To support the PM strategy, the current task/chat model needs extensions.
Analysis of what's needed:

### 4.1 Task-level fields (extend `Chat`)

| Field | Type | Purpose | Status |
|-------|------|---------|--------|
| `status` | enum | Exists but needs a defined lifecycle: `new`, `ready`, `in-progress`, `blocked`, `review`, `done`, `archived` | **Extend/formalize** |
| `tags` | `list[str]` | Exists — PM owns taxonomy conventions (`prio:high`, `type:bug`, `area:api`, ...) | **Reuse** |
| `last_check` | datetime | When the PM last reviewed this task | **New** |
| `pm_state` | object | PM's assessment: `{ health: ok\|stale\|blocked\|needs-info, last_action, next_check }` | **New** |
| `priority` | enum/int | Explicit priority (`critical`/`high`/`normal`/`low`) instead of tag-only | **New** |
| `due_date` | datetime | Deadline tracking — core to "guarantee deadlines" | **New** |
| `assignees` | `list[str]` | Explicit ownership (users field exists but means "participants") | **New/clarify** |
| `origin` | enum | `human` \| `ai-agent` \| `pm` — needed for the AI quality gate | **New** |

### 4.2 Follow-up tracking (new model)

To "keep track of communications with team members" the PM needs a record of
pending requests:

```python
class PMFollowUp(BaseModel):
    id: str
    task_id: str
    requested_from: str          # user or agent
    request: str                 # what was asked
    requested_at: datetime
    remind_after_hours: int = 24
    reminders_sent: int = 0
    status: str = "pending"      # pending | answered | escalated | expired
    resolved_at: Optional[datetime]
```

### 4.3 Background profile configuration (extend `Profile`)

```python
class ProfileBackground(BaseModel):
    enabled: bool = False
    cron: str = "0 * * * *"      # standard cron expression
    last_run: Optional[datetime]
    last_run_status: str = ""    # ok | error
    max_run_seconds: int = 300   # safety timeout
```

`Profile` gains: `background: Optional[ProfileBackground]`. Any profile can
become a background profile; `project_manager` is the first one.

### 4.4 PM run log (new model)

Auditability — what the PM did on each run:

```python
class PMRunReport(BaseModel):
    run_at: datetime
    tasks_reviewed: int
    tasks_updated: int
    follow_ups_created: int
    notifications_sent: int
    actions: list[str]           # human-readable action log
    metrics: dict                # throughput, cycle time, stale count...
```

## 5. Task Management Tools

The PM operates exclusively through a **tool set** (no direct data access from
prompts). This makes actions auditable and reusable by other profiles later.

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `list_tasks(filters)` | Query tasks by board, column, status, tags, assignee, staleness |
| `get_task(task_id)` | Full task detail including checklists and activity |
| `update_task(task_id, fields)` | Update title, description, status, tags, priority, due_date, column |
| `create_task(...)` | Create a task (e.g. splitting a big one) |
| `link_tasks(parent_id, child_ids)` | Build/maintain task hierarchy |
| `add_checklist(task_id, items)` | Set acceptance criteria |
| `comment_task(task_id, message, mentions)` | Post a follow-up message, mentioning users |
| `create_follow_up(task_id, user, request)` | Register a tracked request to a team member |
| `resolve_follow_up(follow_up_id)` | Mark a request as answered |
| `notify_user(user, message, task_id)` | Direct notification |
| `get_board_metrics(board)` | Aggregates: counts per column, stale, cycle time |
| `publish_report(content)` | Create/update the Status Report |

## 6. Background Profiles & the project_manager Module

### 6.1 Background profiles (new concept)

A **background profile** is a profile that runs unattended on a schedule.

**Background rules (v1):**
1. Scheduling is a plain **cron expression** configured by the user on the
   profile (`background.cron`).
2. One run at a time per project (no overlapping runs).
3. Runs have a **timeout** (`max_run_seconds`) and are killed if exceeded.
4. Failed runs are logged and retried on next schedule (no immediate retry);
   repeated failures put the profile in quarantine with backoff.
5. Every run produces a **run report** visible to the user.
6. Background runs use only the profile's **tools** — no free-form side
   effects.
7. Users can trigger a manual run anytime ("Run now").

**Future modes** (out of scope for v1): event-driven runs, adaptive
scheduling based on activity volume.
